rejected.finding: That the regents never write artificial intelligence or AI anywhere in the August agenda book.
rejected.reason: False, and the deck must not say it. A case-insensitive search of all 307 pages of the combined book for artificial intelligence, the standalone word AI, machine learning and algorithm returns 24 matches on 16 pages. The defensible claim is the narrower one, that the facilities committee's own 20 page document carries none of them, and that is what c19 to c22 set against.

rejected.finding: That the search could be narrowed to the five pages of the UT Dell Medical Center item alone.
rejected.reason: It could be, and reporting it that way would be weaker rather than stronger. The zero is stated for the whole Facilities Planning and Construction Committee document, pages 124 to 143, which UT System publishes as its own file, so the boundary is the publisher's rather than this run's.

absence_finding: WHAT WAS SEARCHED, AND HOW. Two documents, both fetched and text-extracted this run with pypdf rather than through a summarizing proxy. First, UT System's combined August 12th and 13th, 2026 agenda book at agenda-book-full/8-2026AB.pdf, 13,480,609 bytes and 307 pages, read in full. Second, UT System's own per-committee extract of the Facilities Planning and Construction Committee, agenda-book-facilities-planning/8-2026FPCCpp124-143.pdf, 587,443 bytes and 20 pages, which is the file a reader is pointed at because it is the committee document rather than the whole book. HOW THE ITEM WAS TOLD APART FROM THE REST. UT System publishes each committee's pages as a separate file, so the boundary is the publisher's own and not a guess at page breaks. Within the combined book the UT Dell Medical Center item was independently located at PDF printed pages 130 to 134, with its table of contents entry at page 123. WHAT WAS FOUND. A case-insensitive search for artificial intelligence, the standalone word AI, machine learning and algorithm returns ZERO matches in all 20 pages of the facilities committee document, and zero on printed pages 130 to 134 of the combined book, which is the same text reached two ways. THE STRONGER HALF. The same combined book returns 24 matches on 16 other pages, among them a medical branch amendment whose own title reads to provide AI technology platform at Funds: $9,850,000, an audit committee plan naming a focus on the use of artificial intelligence, and investment company budget material about new AI tools. The finance committee's own extract, agenda-book-finance-planning/8-2026FAPCpp46-111.pdf at 66 pages, returns 7 matches. So the board writes the word. It writes it in the same book, on the same two days, about a contract two orders of magnitude smaller. It does not write it in the item that carries this hospital. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. Nothing here is a claim about intent. A board resolution is a legal instrument and its restraint may be drafting practice rather than doubt, and the deck says so rather than deciding for the reader. PAGE NUMBERING, CORRECTED IN THIS RUN. An earlier pass in this run located the item at pages 129 to 133, which were PDF page indices from a text extraction and not the book's own folios. The document numbers its own pages in a running footer, and that footer puts the recommendation on 130 and the milestone list on 134. The combined book's table of contents gives 130 for the same item, which is the second source that settles it. Every page number published anywhere in this deck is the document's own, quoted from its footer.
